events.credibility_reason: A search summary of the 2026 LICS paper (Bojanczyk, Casares, Manthe, Parys) reportedly says the authors could not confirm the correctness of Dzamonja's announced proof; Definition 2.12 was changed after v1, with four revisions in under a month. No specific error is identified, so the event is not knocked down.

why: The statement asks two questions, BMTO and MTWO (F3), so a proof that BMTO is decidable is a case, not the whole problem. Nothing in the record touches MTWO. Manthe's preprint claims BMTO is decidable. I scored it unreviewed: Gurevich and Hieronymi are thanked for proofreading in the acknowledgements, but neither has said anything in public about checking it, and an acknowledgement alone is not digestion. It counts as credible because no specific doubt is recorded against it. Dzamonja's preprint makes the same claim by a different method. It is kept as doubtful because of the reported 'could not confirm' remark in the LICS paper and the early revisions to Definition 2.12. The record gives that remark only through a search summary and names no specific error, so I did not knock the preprint down. Her Grok declaration describes help with references, LaTeX and English, and explicitly denies any use of Grok for mathematics, so its AI role is none. The LICS paper is about the 2^(<=omega) tree, a different structure, so it is a variant. Jerabek's note is about the first-order theory of well-orders, also a variant. The pre-snapshot papers are either changed questions (Rabin on F_sigma sets, the unrestricted theory, omega_2) or Shelah's paper posing the problem (none). None of them resolves the problem, so none of them can make it open_stale.
doubts: The LICS paper's statement about Dzamonja's proof comes only from a search summary, so its exact wording and which version of her preprint it refers to are unverified. The record does not say what changed in Manthe's v2 (March 2026). The verification answers for the pre-snapshot journal papers are given for completeness and have no effect on the status.
